ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #20
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. No full stops
   B. Only one word repeated
   C. Many unrelated topics with no link
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

2. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. blue
   B. quickly
   C. run
   D. happiness

3. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word classes: Main and Auxiliary Verbs ● Primary auxiliarie, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word classes: Main and Auxiliary Verbs ● Primary auxiliarie.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word classes: Main and Auxiliary Verbs ● Primary auxiliarie.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word classes: Main and Auxiliary Verbs ● Primary auxiliarie.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word classes: Main and Auxiliary Verbs ● Primary auxiliarie.

   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Sentence Skills: Sentence Fluency ● Sentence fragments ● Misplaced.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.4.1 Sentence Skills: Sentence Fluency ● Sentence fragments ● Misplaced.

6. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1Extensive Listening ● Listening for enjoyment and ge, which approach is best? (1 mark)

7. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. A person, place, thing, or idea
   B. Only a joining word
   C. Only an action
   D. Only a describing word

8. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: Fluency in Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)

11. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library
   B. where is the library
   C. Where is the library?
   D. Where is the Library

12. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goes
   B. went
   C. going
   D. goed

----
